Responsibility and accountability.-All the employees of the organization shall comply with these Financial Rules, relevant regulations and instructions of the authorities authorized so by the rules. 4. Principal Accounting Officer (PAO).-The Secretary Commerce shall act as the Principal Accounting Officer in respect of financial management of the Organization. 5. Duties and responsibilities of PAO.-The PAO, assisted by the Director General, shall ensure that financial considerations and prudence are taken into account at all levels in financial management dnd policy decisions. He shall also look after the matters relating to Public Accounts besides attending its meetihgs in accordance with para-7 of Financial Management and Powers of Principal Accounting Offi cers Regulations, 2021. 6. Duties and responsibilities of E.D (F&A).-{l) The ED (F&A) shall be responsible for the discharge of duties in financial, accounting, and budgetary matters. (2) The E.D (F&A) shall be responsible to arrange meetings of DAC at an appropriate interval to discuss audit and inspection reports of thp Auditor General of Pakistan. (3) The E.D (F&A) shall be responsible for the work relating to PAC, DAC and audit observations on Appropriation Accounts and Audit Reports, ensuring compliance with. the PAC observations and recommendations. He shall 3797 (8) THE GAZETTE OF PAKTSTAN, EXTRA,, SEPTEMBER 3,2422 [PARr U assist the Director General, prepare necessary briefs for the PAC and DAC and attend the meetings of the PAC along with the Director General/Chairman. 7. Duties and responsibilities of DDO.{I) The DDO shall ensure that rules regarding preparation ofthe contingent bills are observed and only that amount is drawn which is required for immediate disbursement or has already been paid from the permanent advance. (2) The DDO shall ensure that the expenditure is within the sanctioned budget and if it is exceeded or is likely to exceed, he shall take prompt steps to obtain additional appropriation which includes reporting to the E.D (F&A) regarding need of such re-appropriation and prepa"re re-appropriation requirement in a prescribed manner. (3) In regard to the contract contingencies, the DDO shall see that expenditure is not in excess ofthe contract grant. (4) The DDO shall also have the authority to submit the bills for preaudit and report mater to E.D (F&A). (5) The DDO, along with Cashier, shall be relponsible to ensure the safety of cheque books and cash money of the Organization. 8. Segregation of functions.-The frrrctions of sanctioning expenditure for release of payments and disbursements and recording thereof shall be separate and eotrusted to different officers of the Organization and as revised by the PAO from time to time. 9. Financial propriety.-Every officer of the Organization who is authorized to incur expenditure from the fund shall: (I) exercise the same vigilance in respect of the expenditure as a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in respect of the expenditure of his own money; (D ensure that the expenditure is not prima-facie more than the judicious requirement of the occasion; (III) not to pass an order that will be directly or indirectly in his / her own benefit except with the prior approval of higher authority in writing; ensure that the Organization's money is expended not for the benefit of a particular employee or class of employees unless admissible in accordance with the Service Rules of ,the Organization; . Allocation.-The allocation approved by the Board shall constitute an authorization to the Chairman and with his consent to the Director General to fulfill obligations and sanctioning the payments, expenditures and financial releases to the extent as may be determined and recorded appropriately. Utilization of fund.--The Fund shall be utilized by the Organization to meet charges in connection with is functions under the Act, including: (a) payment of salaries, contributory provident fund (CPF), loans and advances, staff welfare assistance package, and other remuneration to the Chairman, Director General', officers, employees, contingent and daily wage employees, experts and consultants of the Organization; (b) payment against hired services of and for the Organization; (c) purchase of movable and immovable assets in the name of the Organization; (d) investment in various profitable financial instruments; (e) workshops, seminars and other events arranged by the Organization regarding intellectual property rights; (0 promotion of education and research in the field of intellectual property; (g) raising awareness about intellectual property issues through print and electronic media; and (h) intellectual property through advocacy. 22. (2) Accounts shall conform to the accounting period, which shall be financial year commencing from lst July each year to 30th day of June in the following year. (3) Experrses shall be booked when incurred regardless of actual payment and revenue shall be booked wtren earned or become due regardless of actual receipt. (4) All transactions in foreign currencies shall be converted into Rupees at the official exchange rate prevailing on'the date of transaction and all balances in the foreign ctrrency account shall be cbnverted into Rupees at the official exchange rate prevailing on the date ofBalance sheet. (5) Any difference in the balance ofthe corresponding Rupee account and balances in the foreign curency account converted into Rupee on the date of the Balance Sheet shall be realized as exchange gain or loss as the ca5e may be and shall be applied.against or charged to the financial expenses. The Accounts Officer of the Finance and Accounts Wing shall prepare and maintain one or more books of accounts indicating the daily rates of Rupee against major currencies and gain or loss on account of fluctuation in currency rates. (6) Any expenditure, the benefit of which is confined only to the accounting year in which it is incurred, shall be treated as revenue expenditure and charged to the said accounting year. (7) Any expenditure, the benefit of which extends over one year purchase is less than the value limit fixed by the Organization, from time to time, which shall, for the time being, be Rupees two thousand, shall be treated as revenue exlenditure and charged to the said accounting year. The store record for these expenses shall, however, be maintained for control purpose. (8) Any expenditure, over a value limit fixed by the Organization, from time to time, which, for the time being, shall be Rupees two thousand and the benefit of which extends beyond the accounting year in which it is incurred, shall be treated as capital expenditure and charged through depreciation or amortization, as the case be, at rates prescribed by the Organization from time to time. 40. (3) The following book of accounts shall normally be maintained; (a) cash book; (b) bank books; (c) general ledger; (d) sub ledger; (e) assets register; and (0 such other books as may be required.
